kjv: Would God that we had died
note: Hebrew velu is a simple wish particle ("if only"); there is no word for God, and the KJV idiom may now be read as an appeal to God.
Hebrew mal'akh means messenger, human or divine; addressed to Edom, the phrase may refer to Moses or to the angel of Exodus 14:19.

kjv: by the coast of the land of Edom
mine: on the border of the land of Edom
note: Hebrew gevul means border/territory; Mount Hor is inland, and "coast" in 1611 meant boundary (recurs in Num 20-22, 32).
